questions.statement: Choose the correct separation of the phrasal verb: 'Please turn ___ the light before you leave.'
questions.context: Semana W29 de ingles, grado 11: ejercicio 1 de 20 sobre separable phrasal verbs.

options.text: off the light
options.feedback: Correct! A transitive phrasal verb can be separated, so the object 'the light' goes between the verb and the particle.

options.text: the light off
options.feedback: No. The object cannot come before the verb; the particle must stay attached to the verb.

options.text: off turn the light
options.feedback: No. 'Off turn' reverses the order of the verb and the particle.

options.text: the off light
options.feedback: No. 'The off light' would make 'off' part of the noun phrase, which changes the meaning entirely.

questions.explanation:
A transitive phrasal verb can be separated, so the object 'the light' goes between the verb and the particle. In this item the choice that works is 'off the light', because it is the option that matches what the sentence and the task require.

options.text: She picked book the up from the table.
options.feedback: No. 'Book the up' puts the object before the verb, which English does not allow here.

The direct object 'the book' is placed between the verb and the particle, which is the separable pattern. In this item the choice that works is 'She picked the book up from the table.', because it is the option that matches what the sentence and the task require.

questions.statement: When can a transitive phrasal verb NOT be separated?
questions.context: Semana W29 de ingles, grado 11: ejercicio 4 de 20 sobre separable phrasal verbs.

options.text: When the particle itself is a pronoun, such as in 'pick it up'.
options.feedback: Correct! A pronoun object has to stay in front of the particle, so 'pick it up' and not 'pick up it'.

options.text: When the verb is followed by an article, such as in 'turn the off'.
options.feedback: No. 'Turned off the light' would separate the object, which is fully allowed for a noun object.

options.text: When the object is longer than two words, such as in 'clean the whole kitchen up'.
options.feedback: No. 'Clean the whole kitchen up' is a perfectly normal separation, since the object is a noun phrase.

options.text: When the verb is in the past tense, such as in 'looked after her up'.
options.feedback: No. The past tense of the verb has no effect on whether the object can be separated.

questions.explanation:
A pronoun object has to stay in front of the particle, so 'pick it up' and not 'pick up it'. In this item the choice that works is 'When the particle itself is a pronoun, such as in 'pick it up'.', because it is the option that matches what the sentence and the task require.
